text:
mike: Quick follow-up from the design sync — I put together a compact proposal for a soft-grace flow when tenant credit pools get thin. Idea: prefer local mitigations (kv-cache, model-fallback) then short-lived borrow from a global grace pool, then route deprioritization before rejecting.

sophia: This sounds good. What's the expected latency impact of a borrow RPC for tail requests?

mike: Borrow RPC should be O(1) in the fast-path: central allocator with hot local caches. Cache miss -> single RPC (~1-3ms p99 within region). We keep borrow tokens tiny (TTL short) to avoid long-lived state.

raj: How do we prevent tenants from gaming the borrow? They could hit borrow constantly to get better-than-their-plan throughput.

linh: We should add a sliding-window limiter + decaying counter per-tenant. Borrow allowed only if borrowed_in_window < window_cap and tenant_abuse_score < threshold.

zach: And what increments tenant_abuse_score? Existing signals?

mike: Reuse existing abuse signals (spike patterns, suspicious API patterns) + new borrow-specific heuristics: borrow_to_success ratio, repeated borrow attempts with no user-visible success. Score decays over time. No immediate hard block 1 - probation first.

tara: For rollout we want dry-run mode that logs the fallback decision but does not alter routing. Also want a canary flag per-tenant to opt-in.

ops-bot: note: deploy-check: policy/soft-grace small-diff -> /deploys/policy-soft-grace-diff-01

sophia: We also need clear SLO annotations so product teams know which routes can be degraded. Propose: per-route metadata: {priority: "high|normal|low", degradeable: true/false, expected_99p_cost_change: +Nms}.

raj: Who owns route priority mapping? It's risky to leave manual tags. Could we infer priority from route annotations + recent error impact (e.g., auth failures = high)?

linh: I prefer hybrid: allow explicit overrides, but default to inferred priority based on recent success/importance signals. This reduces ops burden.

zach: Interface boundary: evaluator returns a minimal tuple: {decision: "ok|borrow|degrade|deny", want_tokens: N, degrade_targets: [route_ids], code: "FALLBACK_x"}. Keep it compact. Runtime chooses exact variant and emits header for SDKs.

mike: Agree. We'll standardize header: X-Redwood-Fallback-Code and X-Redwood-Borrow-Tokens when applicable. SDKs surface these to users.

raj: Observability: publish metrics and traces for these fields: fallback_decision, borrow_tokens, borrow_latency, fallback_step (kv-cache/variant/borrow/degrade), tenant_borrow_attempts_window. Also add a histogram for TTL expirations.

linh: Add trace spans labeled fallback.step and attach a tag saving token_delta. Also emit logs in dry-run mode showing "would_borrow" decisions.

ops-bot: test-plan scheduled: synthetic-bursts.2024-09-20T03:00Z

sophia: Abuse mitigations detail: cooldown per-tenant (e.g., 60s) after N borrows in M seconds, progressive backoff on borrow weight, and a global circuit-breaker if borrow rate across system exceeds a threshold.

zach: Edge-case: what if a tenant has many low-priority routes and uses borrow repeatedly across them 1 sum could exceed per-tenant cap. Need per-tenant global counters plus per-route counters.

mike: We'll enforce per-tenant cap + per-route subcap. Policy config example (pseudo):
```json
{"grace_pool": {"total_tokens": 200000, "per_tenant_max": 10000, "ttl_seconds": 20, "borrow_window_seconds": 60, "borrow_limit_in_window": 5}, "route_defaults": {"priority_infer": true}}
```

raj: TTL 20s seems reasonable. Suggest borrow_limit_in_window default 5 but configurable per-tier.

linh: Also we should ensure idempotency: borrow receipts with short nonce so retries don't double count.

ops-bot: note: added lint rule -> policy configs must include dry_run boolean.

mike: Implementation plan: 1) evaluator + local cache proto 2) central allocator w/ per-tenant sliding counters & receipts 3) runtime wiring for header emission & variant mapping 4) telemetry + dry-run.

sophia: Acceptance criteria: no regression in 99p latency for routes with priority=high under canary; dashboards for borrow rates; and no increase in safety incidents during canary.

zach: Tests: unit tests for window counters, e2e with synthetic bursts, chaos test where allocator is slow to validate fallback to degrade path.

mike: I'll draft the RFC today: config schema, API shape, example prom queries, rollout checklist. Raj coordinate canary tenants and tests, Linh specs telemetry.

tara: Add a short FAQ in the RFC: "Why not let runtime always pick cheaper variant?" Answer: we prefer local routing for latency but want global fairness controls and observability, so evaluator keeps decisions minimal and runtime chooses concrete variants.

raj: Timeline? RFC by EOW, canary next week if no blockers.

mike: Yes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
